object.type: curved terracotta tumescent phallus made for insertion into a figure
object.date: 4th century BC to 2nd century AD (museum range)
object.manufacture: hand-modelled micaceous brown Nile silt; traces of red paint over white dressing; root damaged

source_bound_facts: British Museum explicitly identifies the object as a terracotta phallus made for insertion into a mould-made figure.
The object is hand-modelled, not described as mould-made.
The public catalogue does not describe this specific object as hollow or solid.
The root is damaged, creating a potentially informative break surface for conservation examination.

A related British Museum object 1973,0501.45 explicitly states that both figure and inserted phallus were made in two-piece moulds and are hollow, showing that the catalogue does record hollow construction when known.

Another related object 1973,0501.22 is a much larger terracotta phallus probably applied to a Harpocrates figure, showing that detachable/applied terracotta phalli form a broader ritual/figurine technology rather than an Osiris-specific object class.

hypotheses.statement: 1973,0501.23 is a simple hand-modelled terracotta insert with no internal cavity or secondary content.
The object contains an intentional internal void due to manufacturing technique or weight reduction.
A distinct internal core, packet, metal element, organic inclusion, or separate object is enclosed within the terracotta body.
The object contains a physical relic of Osiris.
hypotheses.reason: No Osirian attribution, Mendes provenance, reliquary wording, internal anomaly, imaging evidence, or independent relic linkage is currently source-bound for this object.

important_context.reason: British Museum records multiple Late/Ptolemaic/Roman Egyptian terracotta phallic figures and separate inserted phalli, including 1973,0501.22, 1973,0501.23 and 1973,0501.45.
important_context.reason_osiris: The museum record does not identify 1973,0501.23 as Osiris; probable findspot is Naukratis, not Mendes.

steps: request/check existing British Museum conservation photography of the damaged root
check whether the break surface exposes a homogeneous ceramic core, void, or distinct inclusion
obtain existing X-radiograph or micro-CT if already performed
if no imaging exists, propose non-destructive X-radiography or micro-CT through museum conservation channels
compare density and wall profile with known hollow inserted phallus 1973,0501.45
do not drill, cut, sample, open, or physically alter the object
best_non_destructive_test.positive_signal: distinct internal object/packet, anomalous dense core, nested cavity, or intentionally sealed heterogeneous inclusion
best_non_destructive_test.negative_signal: uniform ceramic density or ordinary manufacturing void without separate content
